kept.excerpt: Tickets for the 2026 US Open are now on sale, with 22 days of tennis and entertainment scheduled for August 23-September 13—eight of which feature free grounds admission—this year’s US Open is set to feature the largest event schedule and most competition days in the US Open’s near-150-year history.
kept.relevance: Confirms the official tournament window specified in the resolution rules.

kept.excerpt: First up in Arthur Ashe Stadium, world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka begins her attempt to clinch the US Open three-peat against Colombia’s Camila Osorio. Up 2-0 in their head-to-head, the signs are overwhelmingly positive for Sabalenka’s army of fans, because the top seed has won her previous 23 consecutive Grand Slam first round matches, last losing one to Carla Suarez Navarro at the 2020 Australian Open.
kept.relevance: Provides official cutoff-day confirmation that Sabalenka was scheduled to begin her singles campaign on August 31, alongside her opening-opponent record and first-round history.

kept.excerpt: Two-time defending champion and No. 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka will open against Camila Osorio. Sabalenka, who is seeking her fourth title of the season, anchors a first quarter that also includes Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. The World No. 1 could face No. 27 Barbora Krejcikova in the third round, No. 15 Diana Shnaider or No. 20 Maja Chwalinska in the fourth round and No. 6 Linda Noskova in the quarterfinals.
kept.relevance: Documents Sabalenka’s seed and prospective draw difficulty before any of her tournament matches.

kept.excerpt: Becoming only the fifth woman to win the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back, Sabalenka emphasised her position as the dominant player on the WTA Tour and created a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings. Two-time defending champion Sabalenka returns to New York with a 17-7 win-loss record since the Miami triumph, including a chastening French Open quarter-final exit and a disheartening defeat in the Wimbledon fourth round.
kept.publisher: BBC Sport — Jonathan Jurejko, syndicated by Yahoo
kept.relevance: Balances her early-season hard-court strength against her more recent deterioration in results as of the experiment date.

kept.excerpt: With an upset 7-6 (7), 6-4 win over World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka Wednesday night, Bejlek advanced to the quarterfinals of the Cincinnati Open, earning her first win of a top ranked player on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. Sabalenka's serve -- usually a reliable weapon for the World No. 1 -- was not up to the mark Wednesday. She recorded four double faults against zero aces, landing just half of her first serves in and winning just 61% of those points.
kept.relevance: Supplies concrete evidence of Sabalenka’s recent hard-court vulnerability and serving performance in a major US Open warm-up event.

kept.excerpt: Elena Rybakina's stay at the Cincinnati Open -- and current quest to dethrone Aryna Sabalenka at the top of the PIF WTA Rankings --- ended on Thursday night when she was forced to retire from her quarterfinal match against Iga Swiatek with a left ankle injury. After Sabalenka lost to Sara Bejlek in the fourth round on Wednesday, Rybakina needed to reach the final in Cincinnati to take the World No. 1 ranking.
kept.relevance: Identifies a recent injury affecting a leading rival, without assuming either recovery or withdrawal by the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Coco Gauff enters the US Open after winning her first title of the season in Cincinnati, while runner-up Jessica Pegula continues a strong summer that included runner-up appearances in Washington, D.C. and Cincinnati. Rybakina enters the US Open at No. 1 on the WTA Finals Leaderboard. She advanced to the final in Toronto and the quarterfinals in Cincinnati, where both her runs ended against Iga Swiatek.
kept.relevance: Establishes the recent form of several principal challengers to Sabalenka’s title defense.

kept.excerpt: The singles field features six former US Open champions and 13 Grand Slam winners. Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka will be the top seed for the eighth consecutive Grand Slam. Sabalenka enters the US Open as the two-time defending champion following her 6-3, 7-6 (3) victory over Anisimova to win her fourth career Grand Slam title.
kept.relevance: Provides historical evidence of Sabalenka’s tournament success and sustained elite seeding while documenting the depth of the field.
